rv.q: Director Ramin Gray brings clinical detachment to this shallow comedy about skin-deep beauty

The cast of four took on seven characters with ease, and kept the audience laughing throughout their performance. Although the sharp social commentary is at the heart of the show, the actors’ expert demonstration of fun and stellar performances ensured that the evening did not cross into pretentiousness.

Segal strike the balance perfectly between innocence and malevolence, as Lette’s newfound power sees him inflict the same injustice he once suffered on his colleague, stealing his ideas and passing them off as his own.
